To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have developed a multiple instance learning framework that uses only the diagnoses of a patient as labels, (2) this framework is applied to a large, real world, uncurated dataset, (3) we have shown that the resulting deep learning model achieves clinical performance in the diagnosis of three common cancers, and (4) we have shown how this model could be used to reduce the number of slides that pathologists have to review while retaining sensitivity

we developed a deep learning system for the classification of cancer types in histology images that was trained using only the reported diagnoses of pathologists as labels and that this system was evaluated on a dataset of over 44,000 whole slide images without any form of curation.

we present a weakly supervised deep multiple instance learning framework that achieves high performance in cancer diagnosis using real world digital pathology images and no pixel-wise annotations, that this framework can be applied at scale, and that it has the potential to be clinically useful.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of decision support tools for clinical pathology.
the development of a clinical grade computational pathology system that can be deployed in clinical practice to assist pathologists in their daily workflow.
developing a clinical decision support system for pathology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work demonstrates the ability of deep learning to achieve clinical performance in cancer classification using only the reported diagnoses for training, without any form of pixel wise manual annotations.
this study demonstrates that it is possible to train a deep learning system on real-world data without any curation and that this system achieves clinical performance in the detection of cancer.
the authors have shown a deep learning model can be trained using weakly labeled data and achieve clinical performance in cancer classification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a computational pathology system that can be used in clinical practice for the detection of prostate cancer, basal and squamous cell carcinoma, and breast cancer metastasis to lymph nodes.
deep learning can be trained on uncurated whole slide images to achieve clinical grade performance in the classification of cancer.
we are able to build an accurate deep learning model using weakly supervised learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development and deployment of computational decision-support systems in pathology can be achieved without the need for large annotated datasets.
deep learning systems can be trained to high accuracy without the need for expensive pixel wise manual annotations, which are often a limiting factor when training deep learning systems.
deep learning models trained with weak supervision can achieve clinical performance in cancer classification.
